A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DINO-Foresight. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable, supporting reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original Cityscapes forecasting experiments for segmentation, depth and surface normals, with ablations and qualitative results.

after.justification: V2 retains original forecasting results and adds nuScenes experiments, transfer evaluations, representation comparisons and scaling studies.

M1.justification: The default PCA-based continuous feature predictor, factorized transformer and SmoothL1 objective remain intact. V2 Section 4.2 adds a quantized DINO-Foresight variant that predicts 8192 discrete codes with cross-entropy and decodes them into DINO features. This introduces a limited procedural variant.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates Cityscapes. V2 adds nuScenes training and evaluation for depth and surface normals at 0.75-second and 1.5-second horizons, Cityscapes-to-nuScenes zero-shot transfer, and joint-dataset training. This substantially broadens represented driving environments and transfer scenarios while retaining the original task types.

E2.justification: V2 Table 1 adds evaluated comparators including Futurist, FeatReproj3D, Bayesian S2S, IndRNN-Stack and DiffAttn-Fuse. Tables 2–3 add VAE-latent and 4M-tokenized comparisons. V1's Mask H2F and separate Segmenter Oracle/Copy-Last comparisons disappear. The original 3Dconv-F2F row is retained as 3Dconv-F2F-RGB, rather than being a new comparator.

E3.justification: VISTA changes from the original 22-future-frame setup with separate task models to dataset-specific fine-tuning, shorter sequences and shared DINOv2/DPT evaluation. The reported predictor learning rate changes from 1.6e-4 to 6.4e-4, without establishing that retained experiments were rerun. New protocols include nuScenes rollouts, matched single-layer/no-register quantization controls, fixed-duration model scaling and equal-probability dataset mixing.

E4.justification: V2 adds analyses of VAE versus VFM representations, discrete versus continuous features, cross-dataset transfer, single versus multiple encoder layers, masking strategies, loss functions, model capacity and training-data scale. These test substantially more design and robustness questions. The original PCA and intermediate-transformer-feature analyses are retained; the latter moves from Section 4.4 to Appendix A.2.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or formal significance tests. The expanded discussion of stochastic future prediction concerns possible model extensions, not uncertainty reporting for the experiments.

E6.justification: Instance forecasting scores change: short-term AP50/AP rises from 44.8/23.0 to 50.5/26.6, while the corresponding oracle changes from 56.1/32.1 to 66.2/40.4; the cause is not specified. Original semantic, depth and normal scores largely remain unchanged. V2 adds extensive nuScenes and ablation results and replaces VISTA scores and qualitative outputs under changed settings, so these are not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Equation 1 replaces summation over all positions with a binary future-frame mask by direct summation over future positions, an equivalent formulation. The feature definitions and SmoothL1 mathematics remain unchanged. Metric formulas move to Appendix E, and no new theoretical results or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The central contribution of unified, modular VFM-feature forecasting remains unchanged. V2 narrows the abstract's blanket claim of outperforming existing methods to strong performance and emphasizes one model handling four tasks. The intermediate-feature benefit remains claimed in the introduction and appendix despite losing its separate headline contribution.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive interpretations favoring continuous semantic representations, full future masking, cross-dataset transfer and scaling. Appendix B specifies diffusion/Gaussian-mixture extensions and newer encoders while dropping earlier PCA-replacement and action-conditioning directions. Some new interpretations overreach: Tables 11–12 contain small regressions despite claims of consistently improved performance.

D1.justification: The detailed DPT/Mask2Former recipes and hardware information are largely retained. V2 adds tokenizer specifications, model widths and attention-head counts, VISTA fine-tuning sequence lengths, nuScenes frame-selection details and an inference-runtime comparison. The abstract replaces the direct repository link with a project-page/code link. These extend the existing reproducibility documentation.

R1.justification: V2 introduces substantial positioning against VAE-based latent generative models and distinguishes its dense forecasting task from concurrent DINO-WM planning. Related work also expands its discussion of individual semantic forecasting methods, including Futurist, and connects the new representation comparisons to 4M and continuous generative modeling.

P1.justification: The introduction, contribution list, related-work discussion and conclusion are extensively rewritten around the distinction between VFM features and generative latents. Existing material is substantially reorganized: intermediate-feature learning moves to Appendix A.2, metric definitions and evaluation scenarios move to Appendices E–F, and the appendix structure expands.

P2.justification: V2 replaces the two-column layout with a single-column conference format, consolidates separate comparisons into a broad multi-task table, and adds several comparison and ablation tables. It relocates the intermediate-feature plot, rearranges the main qualitative panels and updates VISTA images and captions. The original long-horizon rollout images are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens validation of claims that v1 supported mainly through Cityscapes results. NuScenes transfer and controlled representation, masking and scaling studies directly test generalization and design choices. Fine-tuning VISTA and using common prediction heads also improves the fairness of the central comparison. Unexplained instance-score revisions and overstated uniform scaling gains remain weaknesses, but they do not outweigh the substantial gains in experimental support and comparison quality.
